deals.evidence: Blackburn Rovers have confirmed that the club has been sold to Venky's London Limited for £23million.
deals.headline: Venky's buys 99.9% of Blackburn Rovers for £23m
deals.summary: BRFC Investments Limited, indirectly owned by the Jack Walker 1987 Settlement, sold its 99.9% shareholding to Venky's London Limited, a newly formed company owned by the Rao family, for £23m (17.17p per share), with an equivalent offer to minority holders. Outside the 2015+ window but it is the current ownership's origin.

name: Blackburn Rovers Football Club
notes: Revenue and the other 2024/25 figures come from the Companies House accounts PDF, which is a scanned image: evidence strings were transcribed from the page and a text search of the PDF will not find them. The operating loss shown (-£21.4m) includes player amortisation; the club's own KPI 'operating loss before trading of intangible/tangible assets' is -£19.0m. Creditors due within one year were £164.3m at 30 June 2025 (net liabilities £128.6m), largely owner funding, but the accounts read give no net-debt figure, so net_debt is null. Stadium: the accounts carry freehold land and buildings (revalued 1995) but no page read names Ewood Park as club-owned, so stadium_owner is null. No deal since 2015 found: Venky's funds the club by loans and share allotments (Companies House SH01 filings, e.g. capital GBP 201,842,484 after a 12 December 2025 allotment), with no stated amounts per injection. Steve Waggott left as chief executive in late 2025 (accounts list him as resigned); no successor or chair found on a citable page. rovers.co.uk is a client-rendered app, so club pages could not be read. Not found: valuation, kit supplier, social followers, honours, chair/CEO.

owners.evidence: A newly-established British subsidiary called Venky's London Limited paid £23m for a 99.9% stake in the club
owners.name: Venky's London Limited (Rao family)

ownership_summary: Venky's London Limited, a UK company formed by India's Rao family (owners of the Venky's / Venkateshwara Hatcheries poultry group), has owned the club since November 2010, when it paid £23m for 99.9% from the Jack Walker 1987 Settlement. Companies House lists Venky's London as the club's only person with significant control (75% or more), and Venky's London's own controllers as Anuradha Desai, Banda Venkatesh Rao and Banda Balaji Rao, each holding more than 25% but not more than 50%. No institutional investor is recorded.
revenue_source_name: The Blackburn Rovers Football and Athletic Limited, full accounts for the year ended 30 June 2025 (Companies House)
